entries.name: Dijkstra's algorithm
entries.definition: An algorithm that finds the shortest paths from one node of a weighted graph to all the others, as long as no edge weight is negative.

entries.name: Dimensions CM
entries.definition: Software for version control and for managing changes and releases of software assets, now sold by OpenText.

entries.name: Direct digital control
entries.definition: Using microprocessor-based controllers, rather than analogue ones, to control building systems such as heating, ventilation and cooling.

entries.name: DirectX Video Acceleration
entries.definition: A Microsoft programming interface that lets video decoding and processing run on a computer's graphics hardware.

entries.name: Disability insurance
entries.definition: Insurance that pays part of a person's income if illness or injury stops them from working.

entries.name: Disaster loans
entries.definition: Loans that help people and businesses repair or rebuild after a disaster, most notably the low-interest loans made by the US Small Business Administration.

entries.name: Discipleship
entries.definition: Teaching and mentoring people in Christian faith and practice, often one to one or in small groups.

entries.name: Dispute management
entries.definition: Handling and resolving disagreements or contested claims, such as disputed payments, between parties.

entries.name: Distance learning
entries.definition: Teaching and learning in which students and instructors are in different places, usually connected by online tools.

entries.name: Distributed computing
entries.definition: Coordinating computation across multiple networked systems.

entries.name: Divide and conquer
entries.definition: An algorithm design technique that splits a problem into smaller subproblems, solves each, and combines the results.

entries.name: DO-178C
entries.definition: The RTCA guidance, Software Considerations in Airborne Systems and Equipment Certification, that airborne software must meet for aviation authorities to approve it; DO-178B is the earlier version.
variants: DO-178B/C (Software Considerations in Airborne Systems and Equipment Certification)

entries.name: Docker
entries.definition: A platform for building, shipping and running applications in containers.

entries.name: DOCSIS
entries.definition: The CableLabs family of standards for carrying internet data over cable television networks.
variants: Data Over Cable Service Interface Specification

entries.name: Document exploitation
entries.definition: Systematically extracting and analysing information from captured or seized documents and media for intelligence or investigative use.

entries.name: Documentation lifecycle
entries.definition: The stages documentation passes through, from planning and writing to review, publication, maintenance and retirement.

entries.name: DocuSign
entries.definition: A platform for sending, signing and managing agreements electronically.

entries.name: DoD 8500 series
entries.definition: The US Department of Defense's 8500-series policies on information assurance and cybersecurity, such as DoD Directive 8500.01 and DoD Instruction 8500.2.

entries.name: DoD Information Assurance Certification and Accreditation Process
entries.definition: The US Department of Defense process, used before the Risk Management Framework replaced it, for certifying and accrediting the security of information systems.
variants: DoD Information Assurance Certification and Accreditation Process (DIACAP)

entries.name: DoD Instruction 8510.01
entries.definition: The US Department of Defense instruction that sets the Risk Management Framework for authorising and managing the cybersecurity of DoD information systems, and in its 2007 form the DIACAP process.

entries.name: DoDAF
entries.definition: The US Department of Defense's architecture framework, which defines viewpoints and models for describing enterprise and system architectures.

entries.name: doT.js
entries.definition: A small, fast JavaScript templating library that compiles templates into functions for use in browsers and Node.js.

entries.name: Dot matrix printing
entries.definition: Printing in which a head of small pins strikes an inked ribbon to form characters and images from patterns of dots.

entries.name: DoubleClick for Publishers
entries.definition: Google's ad-serving platform for publishers to manage, deliver and measure the ads on their sites and apps, now part of Google Ad Manager.

entries.name: Dried blood spot
entries.definition: A sampling method in which drops of blood are collected on filter paper, dried and later analysed in a laboratory.

entries.name: Driver's Vision Enhancer
entries.definition: A thermal-imaging device that lets a vehicle driver see the road in darkness, smoke, fog or dust.

entries.name: Driving
entries.definition: Operating a car, truck or other motor vehicle safely on roads.

entries.name: Drug absorption
entries.definition: How a drug moves from its site of administration into the bloodstream, and the factors that affect the rate and extent of that movement.

entries.name: Drug Quality and Security Act
entries.definition: A 2013 US federal law that set national requirements for tracing prescription drugs through the supply chain and for regulating compounding pharmacies.

entries.name: Dry needling
entries.definition: A therapy technique in which thin needles are inserted into myofascial trigger points to relieve pain and improve movement.

entries.name: Drywall installation and repair
entries.definition: Hanging, taping, finishing and patching gypsum board panels on walls and ceilings.

entries.name: Duck Creek Platform
entries.definition: A software platform from Duck Creek Technologies for property and casualty insurers to run policy, billing and claims.

entries.name: Durable medical equipment
entries.definition: Reusable medical equipment prescribed for use at home, such as wheelchairs, hospital beds and walkers.

entries.name: Dust.js
entries.definition: A JavaScript templating library with asynchronous rendering that runs in browsers and in Node.js.

entries.name: Dynamic cycle counting
entries.definition: Cycle counting of inventory in which the timing of each count is set by rules such as item value, movement or error history.

entries.name: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
entries.definition: A network protocol that automatically gives devices an IP address and other network settings.

entries.name: Dynamic-link library
entries.definition: The Microsoft Windows format and mechanism for shared code libraries that programs load at run time.

entries.name: Dynamics 365 Field Service
entries.definition: A Microsoft Dynamics 365 application for scheduling and dispatching technicians and managing field work orders.

entries.name: E-marketing
entries.definition: Promoting products and services through electronic channels such as websites, email and social media.

entries.name: EarlGrey
entries.definition: An open-source framework from Google for automating user-interface tests of native iOS apps.
